speaker: Doctor
text: Can you point to the exact spot that hurts, and does the pain start before you walk or only after you have been limping? Also, have you noticed any swelling, redness, or warmth over that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; given the location of the pain in the knee but the lack of trauma, can you tell me if moving your hip causes pain, or is the pain strictly limited to the knee joint itself? Also, have you noticed any stiffness or difficulty straightening the leg when waking up in the morning?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE). Although the pain is referred to the knee, the limp and lack of trauma in a 7-year-old are classic signs of this hip pathology, which requires urgent imaging to confirm.
